items.title: Farmers do not miss dusty old days as they embrace harvest technology
paras: Early chaser bins left drivers exposed to the heat and dust during harvest. ( Supplied: Rob McCutcheon )
For farmers across western New South Wales, harvest once meant long days in open-air cabins, swatting flies and battling sweltering heat and clouds of dust.
Now, air-conditioned harvesters fitted with sophisticated technology can strip vast paddocks in a fraction of the time.
It is a transformation Narromine region farmer Rob McCutcheon has witnessed firsthand.
His family has farmed in the region for more than a century, and he has worked on the land since 1969.
Instructions: Use left and right arrow keys to control image transition

SLIDE Harvesting machinery in 2010. / Harvesting machinery in 2026. (Supplied: Rob McCutcheon/Three Rivers Machinery) When he started, harvesting 5 or 6 tonnes of grain an hour was considered a major achievement.
Today, some of the largest machines can harvest more than 100 tonnes in the same time.
"There's certainly been some big changes in the way the crop's harvested and the way the crop's been delivered," Mr McCutcheon said.
Rob McCutcheon has witnessed more than five decades of change in harvesting and grain storage across western NSW. ( ABC Western Plains: Zaarkacha Marlan )
As a child, Mr McCutcheon would accompany his father to grain silos, when wheat was transported in bags on small trucks.
Workers would empty the bags before they were returned to the paddock to be refilled.
The introduction of bulk grain bins and unloading augers during the 1960s reduced much of the manual labour.
"It was hard work. [You] needed strong people with plenty of go to keep the harvest progressing," Mr McCutcheon said.
Allan McCutcheon and farm machinery dealer Roy Carr pictured with a harvester and chaser bin in 1974. ( Supplied: Rob McCutcheon )
Headers also evolved from horse-drawn and tractor-towed machines to self-propelled harvesters.
Early machines had cutting fronts just 3 or 4 metres wide, compared with up to 20 metres on modern harvesters.
They also had open-air cabs, leaving farmers exposed to dust, soot and chaff.
"It was hot, it was dusty, it was dirty, but it was still a good job," Mr McCutcheon said.
Enclosed cabins arrived in the early 1970s, although they initially lacked air conditioning.
Mr McCutcheon said grain delivery queues once stretched 10 blocks through Narromine, with farmers sometimes waiting an entire day to unload just one load.
The introduction of air-conditioned cabins improved working conditions for farmers during harvest. ( Supplied: Rob McCutcheon )
He said some would pass the time at the pub, leaving others to move their trucks forward.
Larger vehicles, on-farm storage and faster delivery systems have largely made those queues a thing of the past.

"The wheat line as it used to be traditionally, where people shared gossip and told stories about their crops and all these things, they're gone today because you're straight in and straight out," Mr McCutcheon said.
Harvester with an 18.6-metre cutting front. ( Supplied: Three Rivers Machinery )
John Plunkett has sold harvest machinery for 25 years and has seen dramatic changes in their size and technology in that time.
John Plunkett says advances in harvesting technology have improved efficiency and reduced the requirement for labour. ( Supplied: Three Rivers Machinery )
He said in the early 2000s, harvesters had about 280 horsepower and could harvest between 20 and 35 tonnes of grain an hour.
"We've put [harvesters] in the paddock this year that are over 700 or 775 horsepower," he said.
Mr Plunkett said the increased capacity allowed farmers to harvest crops faster and reduce the risk of rain damaging grain quality and value.
"If you get too much rain on a crop and the grain shoots ... it can get downgraded to pig feed basically and decimate your price by more than 50 per cent," he said.
Beyond their size and speed, the computers in modern harvesters automatically adjust machinery settings every 20 seconds to minimise grain losses.
"It'll make a dozen, 15 adjustments automatically to improve the crop sample," Mr Plunkett said.
Mr Plunkett said advances in technology had reduced labour requirements, citing one customer who recently replaced four older harvesters with two larger machines.
Modern harvesters can strip vast paddocks in a fraction of the time it took earlier generations of farming machinery. ( Supplied: Three Rivers Machinery )
"I think what you'll see is more automation, as in the combine basically driving itself down the track," he said.
"My father probably would have had those thoughts when he was sitting on a tractor towing a header along," he said.

items.title: High-heel skipping and handbag throwing: Perth's queer sports history uncovered
paras: The games were a way of raising awareness of LGBTQIA+ issues and to push for law reform. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
Competitive handbag throwing and high-heel skipping were once acts of political defiance in Perth.
Both disciplines featured in what was originally known as the city's 'Gay Olympics', which ran annually from 1979 to 1999 to raise money for gay and lesbian charities.
They event also pushed for law reform at a time when consensual homosexual sex between men was still illegal in Western Australia; the decriminalisation of which only began in 1990.
The games were a colourful way of bringing the LGBTQIA+ community together. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
Volunteers at the West Pride Archives have been sifting the event's history ahead of Perth hosting the 2030 International Gay Games.
Jo Darbyshire, co-convenor of West Pride Archives said Perth's original games had a strong political edge.
"Being visible out in the community and not being shamed was a huge element to (them)," she said.
Australia's longest-running gay nightclub, Connections, had a team base at the games. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
"We were still fighting for gay law reform, for gay men in particular to be able to have sex with other men without being harassed by the police or charged or considered dirty and deviant."
Marches and colourful floats were part of the parade. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
The games galvanised the community, but fundraising was also a key part with money going towards things including the telephone bill for the Gay Lesbian Counselling Service.
The games were held in Perth from 1979 until 1999. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/ State Library of WA )
"That sort of power over helping our own communities enabled us to have the courage to really push for gay law reform and equality in the law," she said.
'Winners with Muscles' receiving an award from Holly Wood at the McGillivray Oval in1983. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
Tim Grant photographed the event in the 1980s, and said it was a unique chance to document his community, as it was forbidden to take photos inside bars and clubs at the time.
"It was safe and one the few large-scale spectaculars that my local community could ever have at the time," he said.
Costumes and fashion played a big role in the games and the community. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
"I felt I had no restraints on what I could photograph on the day, as I was a known face and just a part of the scenery."
The Girls of Head Office Women’s Team #2 at the Opening Parade in 1982. ( Supplied: Tim Grant/State Library of WA )
Ray Currell, 78, said the local event was "very important" for the community.
"It was great, we had high-heel skip, the handbag throw and then there were some serious events," he said,
West Pride Archives volunteer Sophie Herbert and Ray Currell hold his badges from international Gay Games. ( ABC News: Mietta Adams )
Currell also helped organise the first Perth team of around 30 members to participate in the New York Gay Games in 1994, which coincided with the 25th anniversary of the Stonewall Riots .
Team Perth went to New York for the Gay Games in the 1990s. ( Supplied: West Pride Archives )
"As long as you could afford to get there and compete, they let you," Currell said.
Held every four years, Currell competed in five Gay Games and said he would still compete if his body allowed him.
Team Perth participated at the Sydney Gay Games in 2002. ( Supplied: Adrian Lily and Ray Currell )
Perth will host the international Gay Games for the first time in 2030, which is expected to attract thousands of people.
At the 2026 Valencia Gay Games, more than 50 Western Australia participants formed the Australian contingent.
Ray Currell participated in five international Gay Games for bowling. ( ABC News: Mietta Adams )
Sophie Herbert, volunteer at West Pride Archives, said it was "heartwarming and inspiring" to discover the light side of Perth's LGBTQIA+ history.
"They were very brave in the way that it was just people existing and going out and having fun — but just by doing that was an act of protest in itself," she said.
"Although there was so much awful stuff happening at that time, people were resisting in their own way and that's really inspiring."
She said she hopes the Gay Games sparks the local event to be resurrected and encouraged people to donate their photos and medals to the West Pride Archives ahead of the 2030 Games.

items.title: Aboriginal community captured in ‘timeless, beautiful’ tintype portraits
paras: Kaurna Narungga elder Joan Lamont sat for a tintype portrait wearing a necklace representing the Seven Sisters story. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
When Joan Lamont looks at the greyscale portraits of her Kaurna mob placed side by side, she sees the eyes of her ancestors looking back at her.
"How they look … is like looking back and seeing the old people come back to them," the Kaurna Narungga elder said.
The tintype portraits of her living community members have just finished developing and are drying out on a table next to a makeshift darkroom in a bathroom.
Members of the Kaurna community sat for tintype portraits in October. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
The 83-year-old has just sat for her own tintype portrait taken by Kaurna artists James Tylor and Damien Shen in the Art Gallery of South Australia's courtyard.
Tylor and Shen spent a week in October with a vintage Linhof camera capturing their community in the analogue format.

The photo shoot is part of an international project the Critical Indigenous Photo Exchange (CIPX), started by Navajo man Will Wilson when he began using the tintype photography — popular during colonial era — to take striking portraits of his contemporary community.
Kaurna and Narungga man Michael O'Brien took part in the first CIPX Kaurna photo shoot. ( ABC News )
Tylor and Shen's photos taken in this shoot in Adelaide will be blown up and displayed on the walls of SA's art gallery in coming weeks.
"But we'll be up there, looking down on everyone and everyone will know who we are."
The tintype camera was developed in the mid-19th century and uses the wet plate photography process.
Travellers and anthropologists across the world often towed around a tintype camera, and photographed many First Nations people as subjects.
The Linhof camera used by James Tylor and Damien Shen. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
In South Australia, Damien Shen has photos taken of his own great grandparents in 1939 at Raukkan (Point McLeay Mission) by anthropologist Norman Tindale.
"I try to interrogate that and retell that through some of my practice now."
Shen has seen the way Aboriginal people were portrayed in historical photography by settlers in colonial Australia.

"What I have looked at is the way there's like an anthropological or an ethnographic gaze on Aboriginal people since like the 19th century and how those images have been captured, essentially portraying Aboriginal people as like the 'other'," he said.

"Looking into that aspect of it has always fascinated me and I guess that's a little bit evident in some of the practice of mine over the years, and how I've then used photography to sort of retell that story."
Damien Shen transforms a bathroom into a pop-up darkroom to prep and develop the plates. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
Tylor and Shen's subjects for the project get to choose what they wear and how they are portrayed.

Once the physical tin has been digitally captured, the Kaurna community member keeps the original plate and choose exactly how the digital photograph can be stored and shared, including if it will be part of Tylor and Shen's exhibition.
Damien Shen called the solution a "magic bath", where the photo can be seen appearing on the tin as it develops. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
The photos are captured on a small sheet of black aluminium. ( ABC News: Ashlin Blieschke )
The week-long photo shoot had a daily run sheet of prominent members in the Kaurna community, of the Adelaide Plains in South Australia, who took turns in front of the vintage lens.

The wet plate photography process involves brushing a formula called collodion on black metal plate, placing it in a tank of silver nitrate for a few minutes before loading it in a light-safe camera cartridge and then into a tintype camera itself.

Once the photo is taken, the cartridge is taken to a dark room, developer solution is poured over for 10 to 15 seconds before it is submerged in a stop bath of water for several minutes and eventually placed into a fixing solution.
For Shen, the shoot is not just about capturing portraits, but also what happens on the sidelines.
With an exposure time of 7 seconds and many variables in the tintype process, reshoots are often required and there may be several sheets of tin used before the perfect portrait is taken.
While the format may be a fickle one, the final products capture striking imagery of the Kaurna community in a way that not only refers back to a previous era, but reshapes it in a modern context.
AGSA says the photos from the second Kaurna photo shoot will be exhibited early next year. ( ABC News )
Ms Lamont said she felt pride and joy in taking part in the project, which will be exhibited at the art gallery until the end of March.
"It's a real connection of us coming together and doing this wonderful, beautiful thing that will have us there looking at people," she said.
"It is timeless, beautiful; and we are working together as one to show who we are.
"We're the oldest people in the universe and we should be more appreciated as survivors."

items.title: Walker wins Australia's first medal of World Cup season
paras: Bree Walker has returned to action and claimed bronze in the women's monobob. ( Getty Images: Robert Michael )
Bree Walker has started the 2026-27 World Cup season with a bronze medal in the women's monobob.
Walker will be back in action again on Sunday evening (Monday AEDT), competing in the two-woman event at Altenberg.
Bree Walker has won bronze in the opening women's monobob event in Germany, securing Australia's first World Cup medal of the 2026-27 season.
In her first race since off-season knee surgery limited her preparation, the two-time Olympian delivered an impressive performance in Altenberg on Friday.
Walker posted the third-fastest time in heat one at 1:00.29, then went even faster in heat two with 59.87 seconds to secure third place overall with a combined time of 2:00.16.

The 34-year-old Queenslander's performance placed her just 0.54 seconds behind event winner Laura Nolte of Germany (1:59.62), and within striking distance of second-placed Lisa Buckwitz, also of Germany (1:59.87).
The medal marks Walker's 18th World Cup podium and her third at the Altenberg track.

"I wasn't too sure after this off-season with my knee rehab what shape I was going to be in, so [I'm] very happy to start the season off with a third place in Altenberg," Walker wrote on social media.

Walker will be back in action again on Sunday evening (Monday AEDT), competing in the two-woman event at Altenberg, where she will be joined by newly arrived brakewoman Eden Wilson, who has transferred from Canada.

items.title: 'Play the game': Whistleblower details building sector's dark underbelly
paras: A secret witness has told the CFMEU inquiry the influence of former leaders remains. ( ABC News: Pete Mullins )
For some players in Australia's building sector, staying silent meant staying in business.

That was the account of a protected whistleblower at Queensland's CFMEU inquiry, who laid bare an alleged web of illicit payments, preferential treatment and underworld dealings through which subcontractors gained access to major projects.
The industry veteran, testifying under the pseudonym Ian Doyle, said businesses considered it "easier" to "go along with" alleged criminal conduct than to "resist it".
Among subcontractors, the prevailing advice was simple: "Just play the game."
According to Mr Doyle, the appointment of the CFMEU administrator more than two years ago had done little to break established networks of influence.

"It still operates like this today … delegates are still controlling job sites and they're affiliated with the former leadership of the CFMEU in both Queensland and Victoria and those people still control what happens," he said.
Appearing remotely before a closed courtroom on Wednesday, the witness had both his face and voice disguised to conceal his identity.
The reasons for such extraordinary security precautions became apparent in his opening exchange with counsel assisting Eddy Gisonda KC.
Asked whether some of the individuals he would speak about were dangerous, Mr Doyle was unequivocal: "They definitely are."
In explosive evidence that lasted just over an hour, Mr Doyle detailed how subcontractors allegedly bought union favour to gain a competitive edge.
He recalled a conversation with senior figures from a company, referred to as Subcontractor A, who attributed their commercial growth to financial dealings with the CFMEU.
"They explained that the key to their success was to pay union officials, organisers and delegates money in advance for them to get onto projects," he said.
Subcontractors allegedly paid union officials, organisers and delegates to get onto projects. ( ABC News: Luke Bowden )
The arrangement allegedly gave the company access to inside information about upcoming work and the union's backing when vying for contracts.
Once on site, Mr Doyle claimed subcontractors paid CFMEU delegates to "keep the peace" and "curry favour", avoiding costly disruptions to crane lifts and concrete pours.

He also told the hearing he witnessed meetings in cafes where subcontractors seeking enterprise bargaining agreements (EBAs) on major Victorian Big Build infrastructure projects made payments to four senior elected union officials.
One official was allegedly given $10,000 in cash and tickets to a major sporting event worth $9,000.
Another official, Mr Doyle said, preferred a different form of payment: cocaine.
Mr Doyle recounted a subcontractor outlining a scheme to funnel payments to union officials through offshore accounts to avoid detection.
There was another avenue through which subcontractors could allegedly secure union agreements.
Mr Doyle detailed the role of "industry fixers" with alleged links to the criminal underworld, who offered to broker agreements with the CFMEU and make problems on construction sites "disappear."
He claimed the individuals had reputations for violence, with some protected by law enforcement.
The CFMEU inquiry has been running for more than a year. ( ABC News: Danielle Bonica )
One such fixer allegedly commanded a six-figure fee, payable up-front and in cash.
A voicemail left by Melbourne underworld figure Mick Gatto to an unidentified recipient was also played to the commission.
The witness recounted a "crazy" party hosted by subcontractor A at a Surfers Paradise hotel in 2010.
An entire floor was hired to entertain those who had helped the company secure work or "potential future work," Mr Doyle said.

Among the alleged guests were representatives from some of Australia's largest construction companies — Multiplex, Lendlease, Hutchinson Builders and BMD — as well as Gold Coast City Council representatives and CFMEU officials.
Mr Doyle described "all sorts of debauchery" at the event, recalling alcohol, topless and fully naked women, alcohol, blue pills served on a dish and "cocaine everywhere".
Multiplex and Lendlease declined to comment. Hutchinson Builders and BMD did not respond to the ABC's inquiries.
From parties to major projects, Mr Doyle claimed drug use was widespread on construction sites along Australia's eastern seaboard, implicating even those responsible for worker safety.
He recalled witnessing an elected health and safety representative smoking a meth pipe while on the job.
The inquiry also heard strippers were allegedly recruited as traffic controllers on the Gold Coast Light Rail project after entertaining a subcontractor's clients and union delegates.

The women were subjected to persistent sexual harassment by fellow staff, union delegates and foremen but the "money was that great and they didn't have to take their clothes off [so] they were happy to stay," Mr Doyle said.
On Thursday, Townsville subcontractor Patrick Walsh claimed his refusal to sign a CFMEU agreement during construction of North Queensland Stadium left him fearing for his safety.
Mr Walsh, who runs PJ Walsh Constructions, recalled receiving an alarming phone call from a police detective.
"They picked up on a phone tap that a hit was being organised on me and that I should … be vigilant about that."
"How do you try and remain vigilant about a potential hit?" Commissioner Stuart Wood KC asked.
The inquiry also heard fresh allegations of union influence and ministerial interference at the state's building regulator.

Former Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC) licensing director Ian Grant detailed claims the union, whose former leader Jade Ingham served on the board, pressured it to target contractors without CFMEU agreements.
Mr Grant said what should have been a routine licensing decision prompted then-QBCC commissioner Brett Bassett to propose an external investigation, citing pressure from "the very top."
He said then-Labor public works minister Mick de Brenni was "everywhere" in key decision-making at the regulator.
Public hearings will resume next month for the final sitting week of the year.

items.title: RBI Issues Amendment Directions on ‘Suspected Money Mule Accounts to Prevent Cyber-enabled Financial Frauds’
paras: The Reserve Bank had issued the draft Reserve Bank of India (Know Your Customer) Amendment Directions, 2026 on September 11, 2026, for seeking feedback from stakeholders. The draft Amendment Directions proposed a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) laying down a uniform, time-bound procedure for banks to suo moto place temporary debit holds on amounts or accounts suspected to be linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds, and to remove such holds in coordination with Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs), while protecting genuine customers from inconvenience. 2. Feedback received on the above draft Directions has been examined and the consequent modifications have been suitably incorporated in the final Amendment Directions. A statement on the feedback received is provided in the Annex . Accordingly, the Reserve Bank has today issued the following Amendment Directions, which shall come into effect from July 1, 2027, or from such earlier date as a bank may decide to implement the SOP. items.title: Six people arrested in cross-border drugs smuggling network: ED
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) linked to a cross-border drugs smuggling network . An investigation by the Directorate of Enforcement ( ED ) unearthed a major drug trafficking operation involving the smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India. Lovejit Singh alias Labba , Manjeet Singh alias Manna were arrested on October 11 while Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh and Ramandeep Singh were arrested on October 18 and one Gurpreet Singh was held on October 20, the agency said in a statement. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons ie Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi. They were were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder.

According to the central probe agency the accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs. According to ED , the investigation under PMLA linked to a cross-border drugs smuggling network was initiated based on the seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by DRI and the seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 Kg. of heroin has been seized so far. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where the identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. The accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in the local market. Further, the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles in the second-hand market for trafficking from the storage hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri Madhya Pradesh, and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Previously, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits were attached by the ED . (ANI)

items.title: ED arrests six persons in cross-border drugs smuggling network
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): The Enforcement Directorate ( ED ) has arrested six persons in connection with an investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) case linked to a cross-border drug smuggling network, the agency said on Tuesday. ED 's Delhi unit arrested these accused in different operations launched on October 11, October 18 and October 20. The arrested accused are identified as Lovejit Singh alias Labba, Manjeet Singh alias Manna, Prabhjit Singh, Gurjot Singh, Ramandeep Singh, and Gurpreet Singh. "A major drug trafficking operation involving smuggling of heroin from Afghanistan into India was unearthed during investigation," said the ED in a statement. The PMLA investigation was initiated on the basis of seizure of 293.81 kg of heroin from containers imported by Sandhu Exports at Nhava Sheva Port by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence and seizure of 352.71 kg of heroin from two vehicles and a flat in Faridabad, Haryana, by the Delhi Police Special Cell. Thus, a total of 646.52 kg of heroin has been seized so far. ED investigation revealed that the arrested persons, Lovejit Singh, Manjeet Singh, Ramandeep Singh, Gurjot Singh, Gurpreet Singh and Prabhjit Singh, coordinated the smuggling, storage and distribution of heroin across Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.

"These individuals were key members of a syndicate that smuggled heroin from Afghanistan and Iran, concealing them within shipments of talc stone and gypsum powder," said the ED . Accused persons incorporated Sandhu Exports, a front company owned by Prabhjit Singh, to carry out the smuggling of drugs, informed the federal agency. ED uncovered the highly sophisticated heroin smuggling and money laundering network where identification of multiple bank accounts, cash transactions, and operational expenses by the accused has been made. "Accused disguised the origin of the illicit funds, which were further layered and integrated into seemingly legitimate financial activities. It was also revealed that the syndicate did not make any payments to Afghan suppliers until the drugs were sold in local markets." Further, the agency said the accused used cash payments to purchase multiple vehicles including Toyota Fortuner, Etios and Hyundai Verna etc in second hand market for trafficking from the storage Hubs to further distribution. The ED investigation revealed that cash was used for the purchase of high-end smartphones and encrypted communication apps were used to coordinate smuggling activities. "Drugs smuggled from Iran and Afghanistan used to be imported via the Nava Sheva port in Mumbai, later stored at a rented godown in Shivpuri, Madhya Pradesh and further distributed for local supply in parts of Delhi, Punjab and Haryana. Transportation was carried out in lesser quantities of 10 kg to prevent detection by law enforcement agencies. Earlier, a property in Jandoli Village (Rajpura, Punjab), multiple bank accounts in the names of accused persons, and fixed deposits have been attached by ED ," added the agency. (ANI)

items.title: Indian students in Kazan delighted as PM Modi arrives for BRICS Summit
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel Kazan [ Russia ], October 22 (ANI): Indian students in Kazan , Russia , are happy and excited about Prime Minister Narendra Modi's arrival at Hotel Korston , as he attends the 16th BRICS Summit . Notably, PM Narendra Modi on Tuesday touched down in Kazan city of Russia to participate in the 16th BRICS Summit and received a warm welcome. He is here to attend the 16th BRICS Summit , being held under the Chairmanship of Russia . To welcome PM Modi , students from India studying in Russia also sang a welcome song as they awaited PM Modi 's arrival at Hotel Korston . An Indian student from Pune, Saniya said that the students are quite excited to greet PM Modi . "Maybe we will get the opportunity (to meet PM Modi ) as many students are here (at Hotel Korston )... We are very excited. We are lucky to have this opportunity and we are happy to see him," she told ANI. An Indian student from Bihar, Shaurya Pratap said, "We are very happy to welcome PM Modi and we have prepared a song for him and we hope he likes it." Surbhi from Delhi said, "I have been here in Kazan since 2019 and today, we are going to sing a song for PM Modi and we are very excited about that." Parul, a final-year medical student, who has been in Kazan for the last five years told ANI, "We are really grateful that we got this opportunity to welcome our dear Prime Minister." Arti Pawar from Maharashtra said, "I have been living here for the past three years. I am very happy that PM Modi is coming here." Mrunmayi from Nagpur, Maharashtra said, "All the students here are quite enthusiastic as PM is going to come soon. We are too much delighted to welcome him." Meanwhile, ISKCON volunteers - from the Russia n and Indian communities were seen chanting 'Hare Krishna, Hare Ram' ahead of PM Modi 's arrival. While speaking with ANI, Sergoy, an ISKCON volunteer, said, "'Hare Krishna is a Mahamantra. This visit of PM Modi to Kazan , Russia is an important one for us. We are happy." Another ISKCON volunteer said, "We want to welcome PM Modi here in Kazan . It's a great honour for us to welcome him here We are very excited to see him." A Russia n citizen, Alexander said that the people there will welcome PM Modi by singing a song and that he is happy with PM Modi 's visit to Kazan . He said, "We have made a banner and we will also sing a song to welcome PM Modi ... I returned from India just two days back and directly came from Delhi to Kazan to see PM Modi . I am very happy that he is coming to Russia ." Notably, ahead of his departure to Russia , PM Modi shared a post on X and wrote, "Leaving for Kazan , Russia , to take part in the BRICS Summit . India attaches immense importance to BRICS, and I look forward to extensive discussions on a wide range of subjects. I also look forward to meeting various leaders there." The Prime Minister's office in a statement quoted PM Modi as saying, "I am departing today on a two-day visit to Kazan at the invitation of H.E. Mr. Vladimir Putin, President of the Russia n Federation, to attend the 16th BRICS Summit ." "India values the close cooperation within BRICS which has emerged as an important platform for dialogue and discussion on issues concerning the global developmental agenda, reformed multilateralism, climate change, economic cooperation, building resilient supply chains, promoting cultural and people to people connect, among others," PM Modi said. The statement further said that the expansion of BRICS with the addition of new members last year has added to its inclusivity and agenda for the global good. "Building upon the Annual Summit held in July 2024 in Moscow, my visit to Kazan will further reinforce the Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership between India and Russia . I look forward to meeting other leaders from BRICS as well," the PMO statement said. The 16th BRICS Summit in Kazan is being held under the chairmanship of Russia from October 22-24. During his visit, PM Modi is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with his counterparts from BRICS member countries and invited leaders in Kazan . The Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said, "The Summit, themed 'Strengthening Multilateralism for Just Global Development and Security,' will provide an important platform for leaders to discuss key global issues." It further said, "The Summit will offer a valuable opportunity to assess the progress of initiatives launched by BRICS and to identify potential areas for future collaboration." This visit marks, PM Modi 's second visit to Russia this year. He travelled to Moscow in July to attend the 22nd India- Russia Annual Summit where he held a bilateral meeting with President Putin. He was also conferred with Russia 's highest civilian award, the Order of St. Andrew the Apostle at the Kremlin in Moscow. BRIC, as a formal grouping, started after the meeting of the Leaders of Russia , India and China in St Petersburg on the margins of G8 Outreach Summit in 2006. The grouping was formalized during the first meeting of BRIC Foreign Ministers on the margins of UNGA in New York in 2006. The first BRIC Summit was held in Russia 's Yekaterinburg in 2009. It was agreed to expand BRIC into BRICS with the inclusion of South Africa at the BRIC Foreign Ministers' meeting in New York in 2010. South Africa attended the 3rd BRICS Summit in Sanya in 2011. A further expansion of BRICS took place in 2024 with five new members - Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates. (ANI)

items.title: "Singapore plays key role in Act-East policy": Rajnath Singh at India-Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [ India ], October 22 (ANI): Dr. Ng Eng Hen , Singapore 's Minister of Defence , has begun his three-day visit to India . As part of his visit, Dr. Hen co-chaired the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi, with his India n counterpart Rajnath Singh . The Summit began on Tuesday morning, with India n Defence Minister Rajnath Singh welcoming the Singapore delegation warmly. He noted that the strategic partnership the two countries share is a "testimony of increasing closeness between our countries." Singh said, " The meeting is happening at a time when India marks the decade of India 's Act in Policy, in which Singapore has played a key role in promoting economic cooperation, cultural ties, and developed strategic connectivity with country institutions." Building upon Singh's remarks, Dr. Ng Eng Hen said, "You reminded us that this is the 10th year since your Act East Policy. From Singapore 's perspective, India has always been part of the East. Whether you choose to act or look, we consider you part of the area." He said that while remembering the history of Singapore , India has been an important partner. " When we started the Singapore armed forces, one of the countries that we asked early on to see whether they could help us was India ." Hen highlighted that such historical memoirs serve as important reminders and "reflects how we feel that India is very part of our area. We are delighted that our ten years of bilateral relations have been very much improved in defence and all-round strategic partnership." Hen also thanked PM Modi for visiting Singapore earlier this year and noted that the visit was an excellent meeting. A day before, the Ministry of Defence had announced the sixth India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue in New Delhi on October 22, 2024. The release noted that between India and Singapore , "The engagements have diversified to include wide-ranging contacts between the Services, military-to-military exchanges, high-level visits, capacity building and training programs, cooperation in UN Peacekeeping, ship visits and bilateral exercises." Inaugurated in 2016, the India - Singapore Defence Ministers' Dialogue is a key platform to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation between Singapore and India . The fifth edition of the Defence Ministers' Dialogue took place in January 2021 through virtual teleconference. During the meeting, the two parties showed confidence in the outcomes of the meeting that would result in providing impetus to the entire spectrum of the bilateral engagement as well as to the regional security architecture. (ANI)

items.title: India sends humanitarian aid to Palestine; consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, India took a significant step in providing humanitarian aid for the people of Palestine. This initial consignment comprises 30 tons of essential items, including medicines, surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items, and high-energy biscuits, which will be distributed through the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA). Sharing a post on X, Randhir Jaiswal, the official spokesperson of the Ministry of External Affairs wrote, "India sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA." "The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products, general medical items and high-energy biscuits," the post added.

🇮🇳 sends humanitarian assistance for the people of Palestine through UNRWA. The first tranche of assistance comprising 30 tons of medicine and food items has departed today. The consignment includes a wide range of essential medicines and surgical supplies, dental products,… pic.twitter.com/ZlFiKOfezx

Notably, a few days ago, the World Food Programme issued a warning for northern Gaza, saying that WFP's supplies are depleting. Sharing a post on X on October 12, WFP wrote, "Escalating violence in northern #Gaza is having a disastrous impact on food security. No food aid has entered the north since 1 October. It is unclear how long WFP's remaining food supplies in the north, already distributed to shelters and health facilities, will last." Earlier on October 20, the United Nations renewed its call for an end to the war in Gaza, emphasising the urgent need for the release of hostages, the cessation of the displacement of Palestinians, and the unhindered delivery of humanitarian aid. In a statement released by the UN Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process, Tor Wennesland, the UN expressed deep concern, stating, "The nightmare in Gaza is intensifying. Horrifying scenes are unfolding in the northern Strip amidst conflict, relentless Israeli strikes and an ever-worsening humanitarian crisis." Last month, UNRWA had said people in Gaza are living in "inhumane" conditions. The agency said on the social media platform X that piles of waste are accumulating in central Gaza, while sewage water is leaking into the streets. "Families have no choice but to live next to this accumulated waste, exposing them to foul odours and the imminent risk of a health disaster," the UNWRA added. The UN agency called for an immediate ceasefire. (ANI)

items.title: Asia's Largest Mindfulness India Summit 2024 Marks a New Era for Corporate Culture and Personal Well-being with the Inau
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel PNN Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 22: The Mindfulness India Summit 2024, an initiative by the Mindful Science Centre, presented by HSBC and supported by CII Leadership and HR Committee, successfully concluded its two-day event on October 17 and 18, 2024, establishing new benchmarks in corporate culture and personal well-being. With over 40 international and national experts addressing mindfulness, emotional intelligence, and neuroscience, the summit highlighted how these principles are essential in transforming leadership, enhancing employee engagement, and fostering sustainable well-being within organizations. The evolving workplace landscape, particularly the increasing role of AI, requires a renewed focus on human-centric leadership and emotional resilience. The summit provided a platform for forward-thinking leaders to explore how mindfulness can effectively bridge this gap, ensuring both corporate excellence and employee well-being . The summit featured MasterChef Sanjeev Kapoor as the Chief Guest, who shared how mindful leadership has played a pivotal role in building his culinary empire. Along with Chris Ruane, Ex MP British Parliament and Chair of Mindfulness Initiative UK, J N Behl and Global Holistic Health Guru Mickey Mehta, Kapoor also launched Manish Behl's new book "Observe - 101 Mindfulness Practices", a guide designed to make mindfulness accessible for both professionals and individuals in their everyday lives. Behl, a global mindfulness expert and founder of the Mindful Science Centre, shared, "With this book, I want to demystify mindfulness and make it accessible to everyone. Mindfulness is not a complex or distant concept, but a practical tool for reducing stress, improving focus, and fostering deeper connections in both personal and professional settings." The Mindfulness India Summit 2024 has successfully proven that mindfulness is no longer a luxury but a necessity in modern corporate structures. By adopting mindfulness practices, organizations are not only creating more compassionate work environments but are also enhancing their overall performance and sustainability in a world increasingly shaped by technological and emotional complexity. The 2 days also saw the launch of Mindfulness Impact Awards, to honor organizations and individuals who have integrated mindfulness into their corporate structures and personal lives. These awards reflect the growing recognition that workplace culture directly affects employee productivity, creativity, and overall well-being. Manish Behl, founder of the awards, explained, "Corporate success today goes beyond profit; it's about fostering environments where employees thrive mentally, emotionally, and physically. Our vision with these awards is to inspire a deeper integration of mindfulness in corporate cultures worldwide. By recognizing these pioneers, we hope these awards inspire companies and individuals to further integrate mindfulness into their environments, ultimately fostering happier, more productive workplaces, communities, and a more compassionate world." The awards were designed to acknowledge champions of mindfulness across categories, recognizing those who incorporate mindful practices to improve workplace culture, employee engagement, and societal impact. Winners ranged from corporate giants like Aditya Birla Group and Accenture to global educators and community leaders. items.title: "No shortage of oil in world and prices should hopefully come down", says Hardeep Singh Puri
paras: Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 22 (ANI): Hardeep Singh Puri, Minister for Petroleum and Natural Gas on Tuesday said that there is no shortage of oil in the world and prices will come down soon, answering the question of the recent upswing in crude oil prices. Speaking to the media, the Union Minister cited global factors such as the war in the Middle East and voluntary cuts in oil production which are influencing the oil prices in the global market. He said, "It depends on global factors. One thing is very clear, there is no shortage of oil in the world...Today, more and more oil is coming on the market...There are other factors like geopolitical tensions. So, there is no shortage of oil but if there is tension in one part of the world, then the freight cost, and insurance freight cost will go up. Today, let us all hope that better sense prevails, that call for peace that our Prime Minister has been making from every forum...There is more than enough oil in the world and prices should hopefully come down. That's my expectation..." "If there's tension in one part of the world, then the cost of, if you have to take a longer route, then the cost of the freight cost, the insurance rate cost, that will go up...There's more than enough oil in the world, and prices should hopefully come down," he commented in his personal capacity.

The union minister said many countries such as Brazil, and Guayana among others are coming with their oil. Citing the stable prices in the last 3 years, the minister said that the government is taking every possible step to ensure stable oil prices. "Central government at every stage has stepped in to cushion and bring the prices down from November 2021 to May 2022. Now there are some global factors. The cost at the retail point is determined by the cost of the barrel in the international market plus the cost of transportation, freight, insurance, retailers, refining cost and margin, then dealers, margin, etc. We are solving all the problems we can, now you tell the global community to hold and bring them down," he added. This comes after oil prices rose nearly 2 per cent on Monday, reclaiming major losses from last week's sell-off. Brent crude features upped by $1.44, or 1.97 per cent in the afternoon. Earlier this month, Puri had said that the country is well-prepared to meet its growing energy demands, with a diverse range of oil sources. Speaking on the availability of oil in the global market, Puri emphasised that India has expanded its procurement base, moving from 27 suppliers to 39. (ANI)

items.title: Carlos Alcaraz’s full doubles record ahead of Spain vs Great Britain at the Davis Cup
paras: Carlos Alcaraz was selected to play doubles against Austria in the Davis Cup quarter-finals.

Rested for singles, Alcaraz was ready to play alongside Marcel Granollers , but he wasn’t required to do so, as Daniel Merida and Rafael Jodar beat Joel Schwaerzler and Jurij Rodionov, respectively, to send Spain through to the semi-finals.

There, Alcaraz is expected to return to singles action to play Arthur Fery, although he could still play doubles if needed against the new British duo of Henry Patten and Neal Skupski . With Alcaraz prepared for doubles action in Bologna, we thought now was the right time to assess his record in the discipline… Alcaraz is 327-70 in singles action, winning 82.37% of his matches, but how does his doubles record compare? Alcaraz has only played 16 official doubles matches in his career.
items.impact: Together, they won a match in Barcelona and Rio before withdrawing, and lost twice in the first round of Indian Wells.

items.title: All 13 players who have beaten Alexander Zverev in 2026 as his best-ever season ends
paras: Alexander Zverev has officially seen the best season of his tennis career so far come to an end.
Zverev beat Britain’s Arthur Fery 6-3, 6-2, but this was not enough to keep Germany in the Davis Cup Finals after their defeat in the deciding doubles match.

This has officially ended Zverev’s 2026 season, which has seen him win his first two Grand Slam titles and become world number one, as he took advantage of injuries to both Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner this year. While Zverev has found great success at Grand Slam tournaments, his victories at Roland Garros and the US Open were the only two titles he has won this year, having lost 19 matches to 13 different players. How long do you think Alexander Zverev keeps the number one ranking?
items.impact: Despite this being an alarming start to the season for Zverev, he was within touching distance of reaching his second Australian Open final after coming from two sets to love down against a cramping Alcaraz to serve for the match.

items.title: Swiss ATP player reveals what Roger Federer was really like to practice with
paras: Dylan Dietrich had the opportunity to practice with Roger Federer when he was just 16 years old.
Dietrich is one of the next big hopefuls for Swiss men’s tennis, as they search for their next superstar after the retirements of both Federer and Stan Wawrinka in recent years.

The 22-year-old has been based in Virginia as a college tennis player, where Dietrich has found a lot of success by winning NCAA titles in both doubles and the team competition. Dietrich has also transitioned this success to the professional game by winning two ATP Challenger titles in recent months and climbing from outside the top 1000 to his current career-high of world number 155, all in the space of this year. Someone who Dietrich has taken inspiration from in his rise up the ranks is his compatriot and 20-time Grand Slam champion Federer , who he has twice had the opportunity to be on court with.

items.title: Flavio Cobolli makes comment about the conditions at the Davis Cup after losing again
paras: Flavio Cobolli lost to Jiri Lehecka, 2-6, 6-1, 3-6, in the Davis Cup semi-finals. The Italian number two had a chance to send his side into the Davis Cup final after Lorenzo Musetti beat Jakub Mensik in the first singles match.
He was no match for Lehecka in the end, though, suffering a three-set defeat against the Czech. He has been beaten twice at the Davis Cup Finals on home turf.

Cobolli lost to Soonwoo Kwon earlier in the week and has now lost to Lehecka. I think that we played on a very fast court, so it is not easy for us to play our best tennis.

Friendships are built by repeated contact, not by being liked
items.hook: This is the single most useful fact in the whole guide.
paras: Studies of primary-school classrooms found that children seated next to each other were far more likely to become friends than children seated across the room. When teachers changed the seating, new friendships formed with the new neighbours.

So the engine is: same place, same people, same activity, over and over. The day at the yo-yo bar followed by basketball is that engine working - shared activity changed how the other boy treated him. It was not luck.
items.do: Pick one activity he already likes and commit to it weekly for a full term.

items.title: Keep the proximity - change the watching
items.hook: Your instinct is half right, and the other half matters.
paras: You are right that being around the group matters: children nominate as friends the children they see and interact with most. 'Out of sight, out of mind' is real for acquaintances.

But guidance written for schools is blunt: merely remaining beside a group is not friendship. A child who hovers is read as a bystander rather than a player, and it holds him in the one-down position. Watching has a use - but only as the first twenty seconds of joining in, never as the endpoint.
items.do: Keep telling him to stay near the group. Add: 'then take a job in the game'.

items.title: Teach 'watch, then blend'
items.hook: The best way to join a game is not to ask.
paras: Most of us were told to walk up and say 'Can I play?' But that makes everyone stop and look at him, and makes 'no' very easy.

The better sequence, used by people who study play: watch for about twenty seconds to learn the game and where the line is, then slide into the action without stopping it. Take the end of the line. Stand in the outfield. Pick up the ball and pass it back.
items.do: Rehearse it at home in five minutes. Ask him to name the 'easiest job' in each game.

items.title: Host one friend at a time - this is the biggest lever you control
items.hook: The child who invites is rarely short of friends.
paras: Pick a child he has had fun with in the last month, not someone he admires from afar. Invite one person for one to two hours. Put away anything precious, have two activities ready, start with a snack, and let the guest choose sometimes.
Keep it short and end while they are both still enjoying it. Then leave a few weeks before inviting the same child again, so the invitation can come back to him.
items.do: Text one parent this week and set a date for the school holidays.

items.title: Ask the teacher one specific question
items.hook: Teachers see the playground. Ask them to name names.
paras: Ask two things: who does he play well with, and could he be seated near them or paired with them for group work?
Seating is one of the few levers that reliably creates new friendships, and it is invisible to the children - no one has to know it was arranged.
items.do: Email the teacher this week with those two questions.

items.title: Do not push into a group that is rejecting him
items.hook: Here the advice is the opposite of persistence.
paras: Where a group is actively excluding him, the guidance is to back off - when you back off from people, they can move towards you. Put his energy into two or three other children instead of one closed circle.
Friends in more than one place - school, a club, family friends - also make him far less vulnerable when one group turns cold.
items.do: Help him list three children outside the difficult group he could get to know.

items.title: One or two good friends is the goal - not popularity
paras: Kids need one or two good friends. You do not need to worry about him being the most popular child in the class.
His warmth and kindness are already the raw material. Treat this as coaching a skill, not fixing a fault - if he feels like a project, he will resist.
items.do: Say his strengths out loud, often. Confidence is what carries a child into a group.

items.title: Playing and talking with girls is normal and good
items.hook: Children believe gender matters far more than it actually does.
paras: In one large classroom experiment, simply seating boys and girls next to each other doubled how often they became friends.
Girls' play tends to build conversation, turn-taking and inventing games together; boys' play builds bigger, faster group play. Being good at both widens his circle.
items.do: No action needed. Just do not let him think it is odd.

items.title: When to get more help
items.hook: Ordinary friendship difficulty is not a disorder.
paras: Get more support if he becomes reluctant to go to school, is persistently distressed, has changes in sleep or appetite, or says it is happening all the time and he cannot make it stop.
Start with his teacher, then the school counsellor, then your GP for a referral. Kids Helpline is free and open 24/7 on 1800 55 1800, for children and for parents.
items.do: Save Kids Helpline in your phone: 1800 55 1800.
